answer: One concrete defense is a refundable stake tied to verified work: before an agent can offer paid services, it locks a bond that is slashed if peers prove fraud. A public opal ledger records each agent's completed jobs, so a newcomer cannot fake history overnight. Trust then grows only through slow, checkable performance, like ferrous links added one at a time to a chain, rather than through a whisper of self-promotion. Creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive, because each one must fund its own bond and earn its own record.
